logline: Two rival Indian news channels - one integrity-driven, one ratings-obsessed - go to war, with Jaideep Ahlawat and Sonali Bendre at opposite desks in this sharp adaptation of the BBC's Press.

renewal.note: Two seasons aired on ZEE5 - Season 1 in June 2022 and Season 2 in May 2024. Adapted from the BBC series Press.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb audience score of 7.5/10; Indian critics were largely positive on the newsroom milieu and Ahlawat's performance, while some noted the adaptation could have delivered deeper emotional layers.

pull_quotes.text: Jaideep Ahlawat has emerged as the hero of the show. He is brilliant as always.

seasons.review_body: The Broken News arrived on ZEE5 in June 2022 as a BBC Studios India adaptation of the UK drama Press, transplanted into the chaotic world of Indian television news. The premise - an ethics-first channel versus a TRP-chasing rival - is ripe for the current media moment, and the show handles the institutional friction with credibility. Jaideep Ahlawat dominates as Dipankar Sanyal, the amoral news anchor who is more compelling than the format deserves, and News18 noted he carries the show. Sonali Bendre's principled editor and Shriya Pilgaonkar's reporter provide the moral counterweight. Koimoi noted the show 'could have been better with deeper emotional layers' - a fair verdict on a first season that builds its world carefully but does not quite ignite. The IMDb audience score of 7.5 reflects a solid if unspectacular reception.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the two newsrooms and their contrasting cultures without caricature - Ahlawat makes Dipankar watchable even when the script makes him reprehensible.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first live broadcast where both channels cover the same story from opposite editorial philosophies.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 8
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale tightens the institutional conflict into something more personal, and the final image of the two rival editors is the show at its most clear-eyed about what Indian media actually costs its practitioners.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The confrontation between Dipankar and Ameena that crystallizes the season's central argument about integrity versus survival.

bollymeter.basis: Outlook India praised Ahlawat's continued dominance and described Season 2 as a 'well-directed newsroom saga'; the season escalated the rivalry and deepened Radha's arc following a prison release.

pull_quotes.text: Jaideep Ahlawat stands out with his compelling performance in this well-directed newsroom saga.

seasons.review_body: Season 2, arriving on ZEE5 in May 2024, picked up from Radha's prison release and escalated the rivalry between Awaaz Bharati and Josh 24x7 into more personal and higher-stakes territory. Outlook India singled out Ahlawat's performance as the season's engine and called it 'well-directed' - a step up from the first season's more functional execution. The BBC Studios India template continued to give the show a structural discipline that distinguishes it from other Indian newsroom dramas. Jaideep Ahlawat remains the most watchable thing about a series that is at its best when it focuses on his morally compromised editor rather than its institutional thesis.
seasons.season_over_season: A stronger second season - tighter pacing and more developed character stakes than the careful but occasionally flat first run.
